memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If anyone is poor among your fellow Israelites in any of the towns of the land the Lord your God is giving you, do not be hardhearted or tightfisted toward them. Rather, be openhanded and freely lend them whatever they need. Be careful not to harbor this wicked thought: "The seventh year, the year for canceling debts, is near," so that you do not show ill will toward the needy among your fellow Israelites and give them nothing. They may then appeal to the Lord against you, and you will be found guilty of sin. - Deut 15:7-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God speaks directly to the condition of our hearts: "do not be hardhearted or tightfisted." Instead, "be openhanded." Notice the vivid contrast between a closed fist and an open hand. Generosity is not merely about actions but about the posture of the heart. God knew the human tendency to calculate, to hold back, to find reasons not to give. He even exposes a specific selfish calculation: refusing to lend because the year of debt-cancellation was near and the loan might not be repaid. God calls this a "wicked thought."

This is a searching word, because it reveals how cleverly our hearts justify stinginess. We can dress up our tightfistedness in reasonable-sounding excuses, calculating whether giving is "worth it." But God looks past our excuses to the heart. He calls us to open-handedness — a generous spirit that gives freely, without the endless calculations that greed loves to make.

The New Testament carries this same call to open-hearted generosity. "Give, and it will be given to you" (Luke 6:38), and "whoever sows generously will also reap generously" (2 Cor 9:6). This is not a formula for getting rich, but a description of the generous life God blesses. And our model is God Himself, who "gives generously to all without finding fault" (Jas 1:5) and gave His own Son for us. When we are tempted to close our fists and harbor stingy calculations, we remember how open-handedly God has given to us. Let your hand be open today. Ask God to soften any hardness and make you a generous, cheerful giver.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is my heart posture more like an open hand or a closed fist?
- What excuses do I use to justify holding back from those in need?
- How does God's open-handed generosity toward me shape my giving?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, soften any hardness in my heart and open my closed fists. Guard me from the clever excuses I use to justify stinginess. You have given so generously to me, even Your own Son. Make me an open-handed, cheerful giver who reflects Your generous heart. Amen.
